, which started less than 20 years later.

alternativeText.text: A map showing the European land claims in North America in 1754. The British has sole claim of coastal areas near the Atlantic Ocean. The French had sole claim over the Great Lakes area and most of what would be considered the present-day Midwest and eastern Canada. The Spanish had sole claim over present-day Florida, half of Texas, and Mexico. Disputed land between the French and British included a majority of present-day Canada and the area surrounding the Appalachian Mountains, west of the British colonies. Disputed land between the Spanish and British included a small portion of present-day Georgia and Florida.

header.text: Between 1775 and 1783, Americans fought the British in the Revolutionary War. Look at the timeline of events in the years before the war. Then answer the question.

alternativeText.text: A timeline of events from the year 1763 through 1777. In 1763, the French and Indian War ends. In 1765, the British Parliament passes the Stamp Act. Many Americans boycott British goods. New laws and boycotts follow. In 1770, British troops kill five colonists in an event that becomes known as the Boston Massacre. In 1774, the First Continental Congress meets. In 1775, the Revolutionary War begins when fighting breaks out at Lexington and Concord.

pieces.text: Even though the Patriots opposed Great Britain's taxes and trade restrictions, it was a major supplier of manufactured goods for the Thirteen Colonies. So, some people thought that independence would create
economic problems.

content.text: Great Britain is our mother country. Our government and traditions come from Great Britain.

explanationText.text: Many Americans felt a kinship with Great Britain. They couldn't imagine the colonies separating from their mother country.

elements.text: As historians examine each source, they ask what details it supports. If a certain detail is included in many different accounts, it is more likely to be true.

elements.text: As historians examine each source, they ask what details it supports. If a certain detail is included in many different accounts, it is more likely to be true.

Historians ask who created the source and why. They also ask how the source was used at the time. They ask if the source was made for a specific audience. By asking these questions, historians can better determine which details in a source are more likely to be true.

textContent.text: In the 1780s, Revolutionary War veteran Daniel Shays returned home to his farm in western Massachusetts. He was shocked to discover that he was being called to court for not paying off his debts. Shays did not have the money to pay his debt because he had not yet been paid for his service in the war. Shays was furious—the state government was punishing him for not paying his debts, but the central government hadn't even paid him for fighting in the war!
Many farmers in western Massachusetts were in the same situation as Shays. When the farmers could not pay their debts, the Massachusetts state courts began seizing the farmers' land and property.

to fight the farmers. The battles between the state militia and the farmers ended with 4 dead and 20 wounded.

In 1787, the Constitutional Convention meets to revise the plan for government.

textContent.text: In the 1780s, Revolutionary War veteran Daniel Shays returned home to his farm in western Massachusetts. He was shocked to discover that he was being called to court for not paying off his debts. Shays did not have the money to pay his debt because he had not yet been paid for his service in the war. Shays was furious—the state government was punishing him for not paying his debts, but the central government hadn't even paid him for fighting in the war!
Many farmers in western Massachusetts were in the same situation as Shays. When the farmers could not pay their debts, the Massachusetts state courts began seizing the farmers' land and property.

to fight the farmers. The battles between the state militia and the farmers ended with 4 dead and 20 wounded.

contents.text: When Tecumseh says that Native Americans need to "check and stop this evil," he is referring to the white settlers who are moving onto Native American land. The only way to stop the settlement is "for all the Native Americans to unite" and claim the land as theirs.

contents.text: In the early 1800s, Great Britain, France, Spain, and the Netherlands each had colonies in the Caribbean that produced valuable goods like sugar and tobacco. But once these countries became involved in the Napoleonic Wars, they could not easily transport goods from their colonies to Europe. Because the United States was neutral in the European war, the conflict created an opportunity for American merchants.
Decide whether each of the following represents an opportunity or a risk for the United States.

questions.text: American ships could be seized by the British and French navies, which did not want the supplies to reach their opponents.
American farmers exported agricultural products to Britain and France, which needed them as war supplies.
American merchants could make a lot of money by carrying goods from European colonies in the Caribbean to American ports, then re-exporting them to Europe.

contents.text: Look back at the timeline. These choices are correct:

content.text: The War of 1812 was fought during the Napoleonic Wars.

explanationText.text: The Napoleonic Wars were fought in Europe between 1803 and 1815. The War of 1812 lasted from 1812 to 1815, so the two wars overlapped.

content.text: The size of the U.S. increased in the years after the American Revolution.

explanationText.text: The Louisiana Purchase happened in 1803 and almost doubled the size of the United States. The country acquired Florida in 1819, which also increased the size of the United States.

contents.text: The other choices are not correct:

content.text: In the early 1800s, the U.S. fought wars against Spain and France in North America.

explanationText.text: The timeline says that the U.S. acquired territory from Spain and France. It does not say that the U.S. fought wars against either country.

content.text: Leaders of the U.S. were not interested in expanding the size of the country.

pieces.text: In the years after the American Revolution, the United States added the Louisiana territory and Florida, which suggests that U.S. leaders
want to expand the country.

contents.text: In the early 1800s, Great Britain, France, Spain, and the Netherlands each had colonies in the Caribbean that produced valuable goods like sugar and tobacco. But once these countries became involved in the Napoleonic Wars, they could not easily transport goods from their colonies to Europe. Because the United States was neutral in the European war, the conflict created an opportunity for American merchants.
Sort the following into categories indicating whether they represent an opportunity or a risk for the United States.

label.text: American ships could be seized by the British and French navies, which did not want the supplies to reach their opponents.
American merchants could make a lot of money by carrying goods from European colonies in the Caribbean to American ports, then re-exporting them to Europe.
American farmers could sell their agricultural products to Britain and France, which needed them as war supplies.
